title: Postmortem & action plan for streaming interruptions after capacity flaps
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 between 16:12–16:38 UTC we observed a production incident affecting streaming responses for hosted API customers. Symptoms included mid-stream client disconnects, truncated partial token sequences, and increased 499/504 errors from edge proxies. Several customer integrations reported degraded user experiences (partial messages, chat UIs showing spinner without finalization). The event correlated with a Dedicated capacity autoscaling thrash in a single region and a recent runtime change to streaming flush/backpressure behavior.
timeline: 2026-03-09 15:55 UTC - Deploy of runtime-1.23 rolling -> 16:10 UTC - Spike in queue depth on gp-pool-3 -> 16:12 UTC - Multiple streaming sessions report partial tokens and client disconnects -> 16:20 UTC - Autoscaler in dedicated cluster started scale-down cycles, some streaming workers were drained mid-session -> 16:28 UTC - Edge proxies timed out idle streams with no heartbeat -> 16:38 UTC - Mitigation patch (revert flush-change) deployed to affected cluster -> 16:46 UTC - Observed client reconnections and stream recovery
root_cause: Primary root cause: A regression in commit a1b2c3 (streaming: change flush scheduling) altered when partial token buffers are flushed to the connection under backpressure. Under sustained queue growth the runtime deferred flushes longer than intended, causing the edge to see long idle periods and trigger upstream timeouts. Secondary contributors: autoscaler thrash removed in-flight workers without graceful transfer of open stream sockets, and edge proxy idle/keepalive settings were conservative for the new flush cadence.
impact_summary: ~2.1% of streaming requests in the affected region experienced at least one disconnect or truncated response during the window. Three paying customers with chat UIs saw visible degradation and opened urgent support tickets. No model inference correctness regressions were detected (tokens themselves were valid, but delivery was incomplete).
short_term_mitigations: Rollback streaming flush regression (reverted commit a1b2c3) in runtime-1.23 for affected region (deployed 16:38 UTC)
Temporarily increase edge proxy streaming idle timeout from 30s to 90s in the region to tolerate delayed flushes
Disable aggressive scale-down for Dedicated pools for 1h after deployment windows (prevent worker drain during streaming sessions)
Customer comms: Sent incident summary to impacted accounts and updated status page with rollback notice
long_term_mitigations: Add end-to-end canary test that simulates sustained backpressure while verifying continuous partial-token delivery and connection health
Implement ordered flush telemetry: counters for partial-token gaps, time-since-last-write per stream, and token-gap histograms
Introduce streaming session handoff during worker drain: allow long-lived streams to be migrated or prevented from abrupt termination
Extend QA to include streaming/backpressure fuzz tests against Dedicated autoscaler scenarios
Add runtime feature flag gating for flush behavior with gradual canary rollout and automatic rollback on metrics anomalies
Update edge proxy defaults and platform runbook for streaming-heavy workloads (timeouts, keepalive)
action_items: ENG-A1: Revert commit a1b2c3 in main and cherry-pick fix into runtime-1.23-hotfix (owner: Diego Alvarez, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-13)
ENG-A2: Add metric `stream.last_write_ms` and alert when > 15s for >0.5% of streams in 1m (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-17)
ENG-A3: Implement graceful stream handoff during node drain in dedicated pools (owner: Anton Petrov, estimate: 5, due: 2026-04-01)
ENG-A4: Create automated canary test harness for streaming under throttled worker conditions and include in CI (owner: Saira Khan, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-25)
ENG-A5: Update autoscaler policy to respect active stream count and avoid rapid scale-downs when active_streams > 50 per node (owner: Miguel Torres, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG-A6: Adjust edge proxy idle/keepalive in platform infra repo and document recommended values (owner: Infra Team, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-A7: Produce runbook entries for on-call: detection queries, short-term mitigations, and customer communication template (owner: Maya Chen, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-14)
ENG-A8: Review deploy checklist to include streaming regression smoke tests and telemetry sanity checks (owner: Release Eng, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-A9: Communicate postmortem to affected customers and update support tickets with root cause & planned fixes (owner: Diego Alvarez, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-13)
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix reverted and deployed in all affected clusters
No recurrence of streaming disconnects in the region for 72h after deploy
New streaming telemetry available in Console dashboards and alerts firing in staging tests
Canary streaming test demonstrates continuous delivery of partial tokens under simulated backpressure
postmortem_notes: Decision: We will not revert the overall flush approach long-term; instead, the team will rework the scheduling algorithm to preserve low-latency partial flushes under congestion plus a feature flag for controlled rollout. The rollback buys time to implement telemetry and robust QA. Ownership for the design revision assigned to Runtime team.
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial incident report filed after correlating error rates with deploys and autoscaler logs.
2026-03-11 Diego Alvarez: Rolled back suspected flush change in affected cluster and opened hotfix PR. Observed immediate reduction in 499 rates.
2026-03-12 Priya Nair: Adding `stream.last_write_ms` metric and dashboard panel; will add an alert rule for the threshold described above.
2026-03-13 Saira Khan: Working on canary harness. Initial smoke tests in staging show intermittent token gaps with artificial CPU contention — will iterate on backpressure model.
2026-03-13 Support: Notified three impacted customers; two acknowledged and are waiting for fix confirmation.
